info.title: AXLR Bots team topics
info.description: A team's topics on NATS, beside the delivery (docs/architecture/topics-on-nats.md). With `axlr-bots serve --topics nats` the control plane publishes a copy of every event told to a team (a bot's, the operator's and its own) on `axlr.topic.{tenant}.{team}.{name}`, and reads what an application publishes on a team on `axlr.publish.{tenant}.{team}.{name}`, which it publishes on the team as the operator, with the rules of `POST /v1/groups/{name}/events`. The platform names no topic: an application declares the ones it reads and writes in its own spec, on these subjects and with these messages. The wire forms are `adapters/bus/topicwire.TopicEventDTO` and `adapters/bus/topicwire.PublicationDTO`, generated from this document; the domain never sees them.

broker.description: NATS with JetStream; mutual TLS and the users' permissions as in docs/architecture/bus-port.md. Both streams are defined by the control plane as it connects: AXLR_TOPIC (subjects axlr.topic.>, file storage, 24 hours, at most 1 GB, a republish dropped within 2 minutes by Nats-Msg-Id) and AXLR_PUBLISH (subjects axlr.publish.>, file storage, 24 hours, a republish dropped within 2 minutes by Nats-Msg-Id).

topic.title: A team's topic
topic.description: One message per team an event was told to, in the order the control plane recorded them. Only the control plane publishes here; an application reads with a durable consumer of its own on AXLR_TOPIC, filtered as it likes: `axlr.topic.{tenant}.{team}.>` is the whole team, `axlr.topic.{tenant}.{team}.order.>` the platform's `order.**`.

publish.title: A publication on a team
publish.description: What an application tells a team, as the operator. Only the control plane reads here, with its durable consumer `control-plane` on AXLR_PUBLISH. The subject names the team and its tenant; the payload's name must be the subject's. A publication refused (done.* and error.* are the control plane's own, an unknown team, a bad envelope, a missing key) is taken off and audited as event.publish denied, never given again; one that failed (the store) is given again after a growing delay.

sendTopicEvent.summary: The control plane publishes a copy of a team's event after it recorded and delivered it.

receivePublication.summary: The control plane publishes what an application sent on the team as the operator, and acks it once that is done.

tenant.description: The tenant, one token: '.', '*', '>' and spaces written '_'. The envelope's tenant is exact.

team.description: The team, one token, written as the tenant is. Two teams whose names differ only there share a subject: a reader checks the envelope's team, which is exact; a publication on a subject two teams share is refused.

name.description: The event's name, its own dots kept as tokens: segments of lowercase letters, digits and '-'. The first segment is its kind: error, danger, stop, warn, done, else info.

topicEvent.name: topicEvent
topicEvent.title: An event told to a team

Nats-Msg-Id.description: The payload's id, '@' and the team: one event told to two teams is two messages of one stream, so the team is part of the key JetStream drops a repeat by. A reader that dedupes past the 2-minute window does so by the payload's id and team.

publication.name: publication
publication.title: A publication on a team, as the operator

Nats-Msg-Id.description: The idempotency key, as POST /v1/groups/{name}/events takes it, required: JetStream drops a repeat within 2 minutes, and the control plane makes nothing of one past it. The stream is one for every team, so a key is unique across the application's publications.

TopicEvent.description: An event told to a team, as the control plane recorded it.

id.description: The event's id, as the team's timeline shows it (GET /v1/groups/{name}/events, its after cursor).

team.description: The team the event was told to, exact.

data.description: The facts, as recorded; absent when there were none.

publisher.description: Who put the event on the team's bus: a bot's run, the operator (the API or a publication on axlr.publish), or the control plane telling a fact of its own (done.task, error.bot, warn.approval).

bot.description: The bot that emitted it, or the one the control plane spoke of; absent for the operator.

to.description: The teammates it was addressed to; absent when it was told to whoever listens.

traceId.description: The emitter's trace, when there is one.

at.description: When the control plane recorded it, RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, UTC.

Publication.description: What an application tells a team, as the body of POST /v1/groups/{name}/events.

name.description: The event's name, the subject's last tokens; never done.* or error.*.

data.description: The facts, a JSON object of at most 8 KiB.

to.description: The members it is addressed to, at most 16.
